match.reason: The closest bank point, A personal and informed reading, is about an evidence-based argued view with awareness and judgement, but it does not teach linking the text to the student's own experience and views, so it is related rather than the same idea.

rejected.title: Making a personal response
card: A personal response links a text to your own experience, feelings and views. It says what the text made you think or feel.
Your response must stay tied to the text. Point to something the text shows, such as an event, a character's choice or a line of description.
A strong response joins the two. It names what you noticed in the text, then explains how it connects to your life or beliefs.
A personal story with no link to the text is not a response to it. A summary of the text with no view of your own is not personal.
rejected.remember: A personal response joins your own view to something the text shows.

a.q: Which sentence is the best example of a personal response to a novel?
opts: The narrator's silence at the party felt like my first week at a new school
I moved schools once and found it very hard to settle in at all
The narrator goes to a party and then leaves without a word
The novel is set in a town and has a narrator and a party
a.why: It points to something the text shows, the narrator's silence, and links it to the reader's own experience. The second option has experience only, with no link to the text. The third only retells the text.
a.clue: Look for the option that has both the text and the reader in it.

b.q: Tariq writes about a short story: 'I loved this story because I love dogs. My dog Biscuit is my best friend.' What is missing from his response?
opts: A link to something the story actually shows
Any mention of his own feelings or experience
A summary of the whole plot of the story
A view that other readers would also share
b.why: Tariq gives his own feelings and experience, but never says what the story shows, such as an event or a character's choice. A personal response needs that link. A full plot summary or shared opinion is not required.
b.clue: He has plenty about himself. What does he say about the story?
